claims.normalizedValue: On March 19, 2026 a threat actor with compromised credentials published a malicious Trivy v0.69.4 release, force-pushed 76 of 77 version tags of aquasecurity/trivy-action to credential-stealing content, and replaced all seven tags of aquasecurity/setup-trivy; on March 22 the same actor pushed malicious 0.69.5 and 0.69.6 images directly to Docker Hub. Each vector has its own maintainer-stated window and this pack keeps them separate: the trivy-action tags, the setup-trivy tags, the v0.69.4 release assets, and the Docker Hub images. Most endpoints are marked approximate by the publisher and are encoded at the stated minute without expansion. The malicious Action objects were never published, so the Action components carry only mutable refs: the seven setup-trivy tags named by the maintainer and 75 original trivy-action tag names derived mechanically from the current v-prefixed replacement tags plus the three unrestored names the maintainer lists; the maintainer counts 76 affected tags, so one name is unknown. The 26 release-asset and 15 image digests and the two network literals were extracted mechanically from the pinned advisory bytes with recorded input and output hashes; CIRewind does not observe release downloads or image pulls in v0.2 evidence, so the digests are retained for manual review rather than automatic exposure findings, and the network literals and version strings are stated in the guidance instead of being encoded because a compact archive cannot evaluate literal indicators. No known-good identity is encoded because the safe objects have not been independently reviewed and v0.2.6 has two historical identities, and the tpcp-docs- repository-name prefix cannot be encoded as an exact repository indicator.
